Therefore affirming divine providence while denying these attributes is impossible. And success is from Allah.

He said: 'And the mazn (rain-clouds).' They said: 'And the mazn.' He said: 'And the ʿanan (heavy clouds).' They said: 'And the ʿanan.' He said: 'Do you know what is between the heaven and the earth?' They said: 'We do not know.' He said: 'Between them is a distance of either one, two, or seventy-three years; then the heaven above it, likewise, until he counted seven heavens; then above the seventh is a sea whose distance between its bottom and top is like the distance between one heaven and another; then above that are eight mountain goats whose hooves and knees are like the distance between one heaven and another; then upon their backs is the Throne, whose distance between its bottom and top is like the distance between one heaven and another; then Allah is above that.'"

He means a spring filled with water. Likewise Ibn ʿAbbas said: al-masjurah is the full. Mujahid said: al-masjur is the kindled (al-mawqud). Al-Farra' said: This returns to the first view, because you say "I kindled the oven" when you fill it with firewood.

Abu Zayd said: al-masjur is the filled; and al-masjur that has nothing in it, he considered it among the words with opposite meanings.

Therefore affirming divine providence while denying these attributes is impossible. And success is from Allah.

When he stood for prayer, he was like a stalk of wood out of fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

A bird was brought to him, and he turned it over and then said: "No game is hunted, and no tree is cut down, except for what it lost of glorification (tasbih)."

When he was near death, he said to 'A'isha: "O my daughter, I have taken from the wealth of the Muslims this cloak, this milking vessel, and this slave. So send them quickly to Ibn al-Khattab." And he said: "By Allah, I wish I had been this tree, eaten and cut down."

Qatadah said: "It has reached me that Abu Bakr said: 'Would that I were a green plant that the animals eat.'"

'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas had beneath his eyes something like a worn-out sandal strap from tears.

The commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 52, verses 9–11:

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the time of its occurrence, saying: ﴿On the Day when the sky will sway violently,﴾ ﴿and the mountains will move, moving.﴾

Al-Mawr (sway, violent motion) has been explained as movement, and it has been explained as rotation, and it has been explained as undulation and agitation. The verified meaning is that it is a movement involving undulation, tilting, going and coming. For this reason He distinguished between the movement of the sky and the movement of the mountains, saying ﴿and the mountains will move, moving﴾ and saying ﴿and when the mountains are set in motion﴾, from one place to another. As for the sky, it tilts, undulates, goes and comes. Al-Jawhari said: "Mara al-shay' yamuru marran" means it trembled, that is, it moved and came and went, as a tall palm tree sways (takaffa al-nakhlah al-'idan), that is, the tall one. From this is His saying ﴿On the Day when the sky will sway violently﴾. Al-Dahhak said: it undulates in waves. Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Akhfash said: it tilts. And he recited for al-A'sha:

"As if her gait from the house of her neighbour
is the sway of a cloud, neither slow nor hasty."

Then He mentioned the threat against those who deny the Return and prophethood, and mentioned their deeds and the knowledge they held, which is "khawd" (vain discourse), which is worthless speech, and "la'ib" (play), which is wasted effort. There is therefore no beneficial knowledge and no righteous deed; rather their knowledge is vain discourse in falsehood and their deeds are play. Since this knowledge and these deeds entail repelling the truth with violence and force, they are cast into Hell, being pushed toward it with a push (yud'awna ilayha du'a), that is, they are shoved on their necks and their shoulders, one push after another. When they stand at its edge and behold it, they are halted, and it is said to them: ﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny.﴾ And you used to say there is no reality to it and that no truthful one informed of it. Then it is said: ﴿Is this magic? Or do you not see?﴾ Now, just as you used to say of the truth that the messengers brought you that it is magic and that they are sorcerers, this now is magic with no reality, as you claimed. ﴿Or is there a veil over your eyes, so that you do not see it?﴾ Just as there was a veil over you in the world, so you did not see the truth. ﴿Are your eyes blinded today from seeing this truth, as they were blinded in the world, so that you do not see the truth?﴾

Then He removed from them the benefit of sight that they had in the world, which, when calamities pressed upon them and surrounded them, they would turn to, making excuses by the passing of the affliction at the expiry of its term. Then it is said to them on that day: ﴿Bear it patiently or do not bear it patiently; it is all the same to you.﴾ Neither patience nor complaint will avail you: patience will not lighten for you the burden of this punishment, nor will complaint move the hearts of the guardians toward you, nor will it draw down mercy for you. Then they were informed that the Lord, exalted is He, did not wrong them by this; rather, their own deeds became a punishment. They found no way to avoid being joined to it. Rather, it became a necessary punishment for them, just as their wills, false beliefs and ugly deeds were necessary for them. The necessity of punishment for the people of the Fire corresponds to the necessity of that corrupt will and false belief and what follows from them of deeds in the world. When that necessity is removed at some point by its opposite, and by sincere repentance, completely removed, they will not be punished for it in the Hereafter, because its effect has departed from their hearts, tongues and limbs, and no effect remains from which it would follow. The one who repents of a sin is like one who has no sin. And when the corrupt matter has been entirely removed from the body, no pain arising from it remains. Even if those will and deeds were not removed, but a stronger opposing force came against them, the influence belongs to the opposing force, and the stronger overcomes the weaker. If the two are equal, they repel each other and each counters the other, and the place of its companion is the heights of al-A'raf between Paradise and Hell. This is the judgment of God, His wisdom in His creation, His command, His prohibition and His punishment: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone.﴾

Al-fakih is one who is pleased with a thing and rejoices in it, and who is content with it. It is said: fakiha (with kasra), yafkahu, fahuwa fakih and fakih, when a person is of good spirits. Al-fakih is one who is in good cheer, and from this comes al-fakiha (fruit), which is the mirth that arises from good spirits. Tafakkahtu bi-l-shay means I enjoyed the thing, and from this comes al-fakiha (fruit) which one enjoys.

From the same root is His saying ﴿fazaltum tafakkahuna﴾ (you would keep on jesting/lamenting).

It is said its meaning is "you will regret," but this is an explanation by a necessary implication of the meaning. The real sense is that you remove from yourselves the tafakkuh (delight), and when the tafakkuh is removed, its opposite is implied. It is said tahannatha when the hanth is removed from him, and taharraja, tahawwaba and ta'atha (he refrained from sin). From the same root is tafakkaha. This pattern (tafa''ala) is said of one who enters into a state, like ta'allama (he made himself learn) and tahallama (he feigned forbearance), and of one who departs from it, like tahARRaja and ta'athatha.

The point is that He, glory be to Him, combined for them two kinds of bliss: the bliss of the heart through delight, and the bliss of the body through eating, drinking and marriage. He protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire, so He spared them what they dislike and gave them what they love, as a fitting recompense (jaza' wifaqa), because they abandoned what is disliked and performed what is loved. Thus their recompense corresponded to their deeds.

Then He informed of the everlasting nature of this for them by what His saying "hani'an" (wholesome, without distress) conveys. For if they knew that it would cease and come to an end, that would spoil their bliss for them, and it would not have been a pleasure (hana') for them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 52, verse 20:

Then He mentioned their gatherings and their postures in them, and said: ﴿Reclining on thrones arranged in rows﴾

In the mention of their being arranged in rows there is an indication of the perfection of the blessing upon them, through the nearness of some of them to others and their facing one another, as the Exalted said: ﴿Reclining on them, facing one another﴾

For it is part of the completeness of pleasure and bliss that a person, in his garden and his dwelling, has with him one whom he loves to keep company with and prefers to be near, and is not distant from him, separated from him, but rather his throne is beside the throne of the one he loves.

(Section)

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will marry them to fair ones with wide, lovely eyes﴾

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "We made them mates, just as a sandal is paired with a sandal; We made them into pairs, two by two."

Yunus said: "We paired them with them (qarnahum bihinna), and it is not from the contract of marriage (ʿaqd al-tazwīj)."

He said: "The Arabs do not say 'tazawwajtu bihā'; they say 'tazawwajtuhā'."

Ibn Nasr said: "This, and the revelation, supports what Yunus said, namely His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when Zayd had accomplished his need from her, We married her to you﴾. Had it been 'tazawwajtu bihā', He would have said: 'zawwajnāka bihā'."

Ibn Sallam said: "The Tamim say: 'tazawwajtu imra'atan' and 'tazawwajtu bihā', and al-Kisa'i also related it."

Al-Azhari said: "The Arabs say 'zawwajtuhu imra'atan' and 'tazawwajtu imra'atan', and it is not part of their speech to say 'tazawwajtu bi-imra'atin'."

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will marry them to fair ones with wide, lovely eyes﴾ means: We paired them with them.

Al-Farra' said: "It is a dialect of the Azd Shanu'ah."

Al-Wahidi said: "Abu 'Ubaydah's view on this is best, because he took it from tazwīj in the sense of making a thing into a pair, not in the sense of the marriage contract."

From this it is permissible to say: "He was single, so We paired him with another," just as one says "shaffa'tuhu bi-ākhar" (I made him a pair with another).

The preposition bi- is only prohibited according to those who prohibit it when the meaning is the marriage contract.

I say: There is nothing to prevent both meanings from being intended together. The word tazwīj indicates marriage, as Mujahid said: "We married them to the fair ones (ankahnāhum al-ḥūr)."

And the particle bi- indicates association and joining, and this is more eloquent than omitting it, and God knows best.

(Section)

He said in (al-Tibyan fi Aqsam al-Qur'an):

As for "ḥūr ʿīn" (fair ones with wide, lovely eyes): Mujahid said: "They are those whose gaze is bewildered, the marrow of whose shanks is visible from behind their garments, and the beholder sees his face in the liver of one of them like a mirror, from the thinness of the skin and the clearness of the complexion."

Qatadah said: "ḥūr means white (bayḍ), and so said Ibn 'Abbas."

Muqatil said: "al-ḥūr are those with white faces, al-ʿīn are those with beautiful eyes. A ʿayn ḥawrā' is one with intensely black pupils, pure whiteness of the eye, long lashes with their blackness, perfect beauty. A woman is not called ḥawrā' until, along with the blackness of her eyes, there is the whiteness of the body's complexion."

Thus He described them with whiteness, beauty and comeliness, as He said: ﴿In them are good and beautiful ones﴾

The whiteness is in their complexions, the beauty in their faces, and the comeliness in their eyes. God the Glorified has described the women of the people of Paradise with the best of attributes.

By what He described, He indicated what He left unmentioned.

If you wish for detail, then what is praised and recommended in a woman's face, body and character is:

Whiteness in four things: the complexion, the whiteness of the eye, the parting of the hair, and the teeth.

Blackness in four things: the blackness of the eye, the blackness of the hair of the head, of the eyelid, and of the eyebrows.

Redness in four things: the tongue, the two lips, the two cheeks, and a redness mingled with whiteness that beautifies and adorns it.

Roundness in four things: the face, the head, the ankle, and the buttocks.

Length in four things: the stature, the neck, the hair, and the eyebrow. Breadth in four things: the forehead, the eye, the face, and the chest.

Smallness in four things: the breast, the mouth, the palm, and the foot.

Fragrance in four things: the mouth, the nose, the parting of the hair, and the private part.

Narrowness in one place.

As for character, as the Exalted said: ﴿Loving, of equal age﴾, for ʿurub is the plural of ʿarūb, which is the woman who is endearing to her husband by her character, gentleness and manners.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: "The ʿarūb among women is the one obedient to her husband and endearing to him."

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "She is the good in marital conduct (al-ḥasanah al-tabaʿdul)." Al-Mubarrad said: "She is the one who loves her husband passionately." Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: "She is the coquette (al-ghanjah), and it is said: the one of charming shape (al-shakilah)."

So this is a description of their characters, and that is a description of their natures. When you reflect upon the attributes with which God described them, you will see that they entail these qualities and what lies beyond them. And God is the One sought for help.

Then He, glory be to Him, informed of the completion of their bliss by joining their offspring to them in rank, even though the offspring had not performed their deeds, so that their eyes might be comforted by them and their joy and happiness be complete. He also informed that He, glory be to Him, does not diminish the fathers' deeds at all by this joining, so as to lower them from the higher rank to the lower rank. Rather, He joins the children to the fathers and fully gives the fathers their rewards and ranks.

Then He, glory be to Him, informed that this is His act only toward the people of grace (fadl).

As for the people of justice (adl), He does not do that to them. Rather, ﴿every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾. In this there is a removal of the presumption of equating the two groups through this joining, as in His words ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾. It removes the presumption of lowering the fathers to the rank of the children and dividing the fathers' rewards between them and the children, which would reduce the reward of their deeds. So He removed this presumption with His words ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾, meaning: We did not diminish them.

(Benefit)

When He, glory be to Him, informed of the joining of the offspring to their fathers in rank though they had no deeds of their own, someone might presume that the fathers would be lowered to the rank of the offspring. So He removed this presumption with His words: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾ [al-Tur: 21].

That is, We did not diminish anything of the fathers' rewards for their deeds. Rather, We raised their offspring to their rank, and We did not lower them to the offspring's rank by reducing their rewards.

And since the presumption may go to the idea that He does the same with the people of the Fire as He does with the people of Paradise, He cut off this presumption with His words, may He be exalted: ﴿every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾.

(Section)

He said in (Tariq al-Hijratayn):

As for His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith — We will join them with their offspring﴾.

This verse indicates that Allah, glory be to Him, joins the offspring of the believers to them in Paradise, and that they will be with them in their rank.

Yet with this, one should not presume that the fathers descend to the rank of the offspring, for Allah did not deprive them — meaning He did not diminish them of anything of their deeds — rather He raised their offspring to their ranks while fully giving the fathers their rewards.

And since joining the offspring to the fathers in rank is only by the ruling of following, not by deeds, someone might presume that the offspring of the disbelievers are joined to them in punishment by following, even though they had no deeds of the fathers. So Allah, exalted is He, cut off this presumption with His words, exalted is He: ﴿every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾.

Consider His words, exalted is He: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith﴾, how He used the conjunctive waw in the following of the offspring, and made the report about the believers who have this condition, so the report was made to depend on two matters:

First: the faith of the fathers.

Second: Allah's following of their offspring after them. That does not require that every believer be followed by every one of his offspring. If this meaning were intended, it would have said: "And those who believed, their offspring follow them."

So conjoining the following with waw requires that what is conjoined with it be a condition and a prerequisite for the establishment of the report, not its occurrence for every individual of the subject.

On this is based what Muslim recorded in his Sahih from Aisha, Mother of the Believers, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was brought a child from the Ansar on whom he would pray. She said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, good tidings for this one, he did no evil and did not reach it (the age of understanding).

He said: "Or is it other than that, O Aisha? Allah, mighty and majestic, created Paradise and created for it its people, and created them for it while they were in their fathers' loins; and He created the Fire and created for it its people, and created them for it while they were in their fathers' loins."

This hadith indicates that one cannot testify for every child of the believers that he is in Paradise, though it is generally said of the children of the believers that they are in Paradise. But testifying for a specific individual is impermissible, just as one testifies for believers in general that they are in Paradise, but does not testify for a specific person of that except one whom the Prophet ﷺ testified for.

This is the explanation of the hadith that confuses many people.

Imam Ahmad rejected it and said: It is not authentic.

And who doubts that the children of Muslims are in Paradise?

Some people interpreted it in distant interpretations.

(Section)

Qays narrated from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Indeed Allah raises the offspring of the believer to him in his rank, even if they are below him in deed, so that his eye may be comforted by them.» Then he recited ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith — We will join them with their offspring, and We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾

He said: «He did not diminish the fathers by what He gave the sons.»

Ibn Mardawayh mentioned in his tafsir, from the hadith of Sharik, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas — Sharik said: I think he related it from the Prophet ﷺ — that he said:

«When a man enters Paradise, he asks about his parents, his wife and his children? It is said: They did not reach your rank, or your deed. He says: O Lord, I did deeds for myself and for them. So it is commanded that they be joined to him.» Then Ibn Abbas recited ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith﴾

to the end of the verse.

The exegetes have differed about the "offspring" (dhurriyyah) in this verse: does it mean the young, the adults, or both?

There are three opinions. Their disagreement is based on whether His words «in faith» are a circumstantial clause (hal) from the followers (the offspring) or from the followed believers (the fathers).

One group said: The meaning is: "And those who believed, and We made their offspring follow them in their faith, so they attained from faith the like of what they attained, We joined them to them in the ranks." 

They said: This is indicated by the reading of those who read ﴿wa-ittaba'athum dhurriyyatuhum﴾, making the verb in the following belong to them.

They said: Allah, glory be to Him, has applied the term "offspring" to adults, as He said: ﴿And among his offspring, Dawud and Sulayman﴾

And He said: ﴿The offspring of those whom We carried with Nuh﴾

And He said: ﴿And we were an offspring after them; will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?﴾

This is the view of the adult intelligent people.

They said: This is indicated by what Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas, raising it: «Indeed Allah raises the offspring of the believer to his rank even if they are below him in deed, so that his eye may be comforted by them.»

This indicates that they entered with their deeds, but they did not have deeds by which they could reach their fathers' rank.

So He made them reach it, even though their deeds fell short of it.

They said: Also, faith is speech, action and intention.

This is only possible for adults. Based on this, the meaning is: Allah, glory be to Him, gathers the offspring of the believer to him when they attain faith like his faith, since this is the reality of following, even if they are below him in faith; Allah raises them to his rank, comforting his eye and completing his bliss.

This is like the wives of the Prophet ﷺ being with him in the rank by following, even though they did not reach that rank by their own deeds.

Another group said: The offspring here are the young. The meaning: "And those who believed, and We made their offspring follow them in the faith of the fathers. The offspring follow the fathers, even if they are young in faith and its rulings, such as inheritance, blood money, prayer upon them, burial in the graves of Muslims, and other things, except in what pertains to the rulings of adults."

On this view, His words «in faith» are in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) from both objects, meaning: "And We made their offspring follow them in the faith of the fathers."

They said: What supports the soundness of this view is that adults have their own ruling regarding reward and punishment, for they are independent in themselves; they are not followers of the fathers in anything of the rulings of this world, nor in the rulings of reward and punishment, because of their independence.

If "offspring" meant adults, then all adult children of the Companions would be in the rank of their fathers, and all adult children of the Successors would be in the rank of their fathers, and so on until the Day of Resurrection. Then the later ones would be in the rank of the earlier ones.

They said: It is also indicated by the fact that He, glory be to Him, made them with them as followers in rank,

just as He made them followers with them in faith.

If they were adults, their faith would not be a following, but an independent faith.

They said: It is also indicated by the fact that Allah, glory be to Him, made the dwellings in Paradise according to deeds, regarding those who act independently.

As for followers, Allah, glory be to Him, raises them to the rank of their relatives, even if they have no deeds, as mentioned before.

Also, the houris and the servants are in the rank of their people, even though they have no deeds, unlike the adult responsible persons, who are raised to where their deeds have brought them.

A group, among them al-Wahidi, said: The best view is to take "offspring" as including both the young and the adults, because the adult follows the father by his own faith, and the young follows the father by the father's faith.

They said: "Dhurriyyah" applies to the young and the old, the one and the many, the son and the father, as Allah said: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾, meaning their fathers.

And "faith" applies to following faith and to chosen, earned faith.

From its application to following faith is His words: ﴿the freeing of a believing slave﴾. So if one frees a young slave, it is valid.

They said: The sayings of the early generations support this.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn Abbas: Indeed Allah raises the offspring of the believers to their rank, even if they are below them in deed, so that their eyes may be comforted. Then he recited this verse.

Ibn Mas'ud said about this verse: A man may have a foot (i.e., an early precedence) and have offspring, and he enters Paradise, and they are raised to him so that his eye is comforted by them, even if they did not reach that.

Abu Mijlaz said: Allah gathers them for him as he loved them to be gathered in the world. Al-Sha'bi said: Allah admits the offspring into Paradise by the deeds of their fathers.

Al-Kalbi said, from Ibn Abbas: If the fathers are higher in rank than the sons, Allah raises the sons to the fathers; and if the sons are higher in rank than the fathers, Allah raises the fathers to the sons. Ibrahim said: They are given the like of their fathers' rewards, and the fathers' rewards are not diminished at all.

He said: The soundness of this view is supported by the fact that the two readings are like the two verses. Whoever reads ﴿wa-ittaba'athum dhurriyyatuhum﴾, this refers to adults to whom the attribution of the verb is valid, as He said: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them with excellence﴾

And whoever reads ﴿wa-atba'nahum dhurriyyatihim﴾, this refers to the young whom Allah made to follow them in faith by ruling.

So the two readings indicate the two types.

I say: Restricting "dhurriyyah" here to the young is more evident, lest it follow that the later ones and the earlier ones are equal in ranks.

This does not apply to the young, for the children of every man and his offspring are with him in his rank. And Allah knows best.

[Section: The child follows his parents if they embrace Islam]

The second category: the conversion to Islam of both parents, or one of them, and the child follows him before puberty. An insane person does not follow his grandfather or grandmother in Islam. This is the position of Ahmad and Abu Hanifa.

Malik said: He does not follow his mother in Islam; rather, following is specific to the father, because lineage belongs to him and guardianship over the child belongs to him, and he is the 'asabah. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith — We will join them with their offspring﴾ [al-Tur: 21]

And offspring (dhurriyyah) is attributed only to the father. Ibn Wahb disagreed with him and agreed with the majority in the following of both father and mother.

Al-Shafi'i said: He follows both parents, even if they are ascendants, whether or not they are heirs.

His companions said: If the grandfather, or the father, or the maternal grandfather embraces Islam, the child follows him if the child's father is not alive, with certainty; and if the father is alive, then there are two views:

The more correct is that he follows him.

They said: When the child reaches puberty, if he declares Islam, what we ruled for him is confirmed; and if he declares disbelief, there are two opinions:

The well-known is that he is an apostate, because the ruling of his Islam preceded, so it resembles Islam by choice, as when conception occurred in a state of Islam.

The second: he is an original disbeliever, because he was ruled as a disbeliever initially, and was removed by following; so when he becomes independent, following ends.

The evidence for his following his mother is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "His parents make him a Jew or a Christian."

He meant whichever of his two parents exists. If he follows one of his parents in disbelief, then he follows them in Islam all the more so.

As for their saying that guardianship and asabah belong to the father, so following is his and not the mother's: it is said that guardianship of upbringing, custody and care belongs to the mother and not the father. The father's guardianship over the child in guarding his property is only one kind of strength, while the mother's guardianship in upbringing and custody is stronger. So if the child's following of his mother in Islam is not stronger than following the father, it is at least equal to it.

Also, the child is truly a part of her, and for this reason he follows her in freedom and slavery by consensus, not the father. So when she embraces Islam, all her other parts follow her, and the child is one of her parts. It is clarified by this: if she embraced Islam while pregnant with him, the child is ruled to be Muslim following her Islam, because he is part of her, so it is impossible for him to remain upon his disbelief while his mother is ruled to be Muslim.

[Section]

He said in (Zad al-Muhajir):

As for the second type of following: they are the followers among the believers' offspring who have not yet attained the legal responsibility in the abode of this world, and they are with their fathers as followers. Allah said about them: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith — We will join them with their offspring, and We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾

He, glory be to Him, informed that He joins the offspring to their fathers in Paradise, as they followed them in faith. Since the offspring have no deeds by which they deserve those ranks, He said: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾

The pronoun refers to those who believed, meaning: We did not diminish them of their deeds; rather We raised their offspring to their rank while fully giving them the rewards of their deeds. Their standing is not like the standing of one who had no deeds; rather We fulfilled their rewards and joined their offspring to them beyond what they deserved by their deeds.

Then, since this joining is in reward and ranks, as a grace from Allah, it may occur to the mind that the joining of the offspring is also established for them in the sense of justice. So when they acquire evil deeds that necessitate punishment, each doer is held in pledge for what he earned, and nothing of it attaches to another. The joining mentioned is only in grace and reward, not in justice and punishment. This is one of the secrets and treasures of the Qur'an that Allah specially grants understanding of to whom He wills.

This verse includes all categories of creation: their wretched and their happy, the happy leaders and followers, and the wretched leaders and followers. It is incumbent upon the intelligent person who counsels himself to consider which of these categories he is in, and not to be deceived by habit or to incline to idleness. If he is of the happy category, let him advance to what is above it and exert his effort, and Allah is the Protector of success. If he is of the wretched category, let him move from it to the happy category while there is still opportunity, before he says: "Would that I had taken a way with the Messenger."

He said: ﴿And the flesh of birds, of whatever they desire﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 21].

In *Sunan Ibn Majah*, from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

"The master of the food of the people of this world and the people of Paradise is meat."

And from the hadith of Buraydah, traced back to the Prophet:

"The best of condiments in this world and the Hereafter is meat."

In the *Sahih* (authentic collection), from him (ﷺ):

"The virtue of 'A'ishah over women is like the virtue of tharid (broth-soaked bread) over all other food."

Tharid is bread with meat. The poet said:

"When you season bread with meat,
that is the trust of Allah, the tharid."

al-Zuhri said: "Eating meat adds seventy strengths."

Muhammad ibn Wasi' said: "Meat increases sight." It is also reported from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him: ("Eat meat, for it clarifies the complexion, flattens the belly, and improves character.")

Nafi' said: "When it was Ramadan, Ibn 'Umar would not miss meat, and when he travelled he would not miss meat." It is mentioned from 'Ali: ("Whoever abstains from it for forty nights, his character deteriorates.")

As for the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, which Abu Dawud related as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet):

"Do not cut meat with a knife, for it is the practice of non-Arabs; tear it with your teeth, for it is more wholesome and more agreeable."

Imam Ahmad rejected this on the basis of what is authentically established from him (ﷺ) concerning cutting with a knife, in two hadiths, which have already been mentioned.

Meat comes in kinds that differ according to their origins and natures, so we mention the ruling, nature, benefit and harm of each kind.

Sheep meat: hot in the second degree and moist in the first. Its best is that of a yearling, which produces good, strong blood for one whose digestion is sound. It suits those with cold and balanced temperaments, and people undertaking full exercise in cold places and seasons. It is beneficial for those with excess black bile, strengthening the mind and memory. The meat of the old and the emaciated is poor, and likewise the meat of ewes. The best is the meat of the black male, for it is lighter, tastier and more beneficial. The castrated is more beneficial and better. The red, fat animal is lighter and better as nourishment. The young goat (jadha') provides less nourishment and floats in the stomach.

The best meat is that which is close to the bone. The right side is lighter and better than the left. The front is better than the back. The Prophet's (ﷺ) favourite part of the sheep was its front. Whatever is higher, apart from the head, is lighter and better than what is lower. al-Farazdaq gave a man who was buying meat for him instructions: "Take the front, and beware of the head and the belly, for the disease is in them."

Neck meat is good, tasty, quick to digest and light. The foreleg is the lightest, tastiest and most delicate of meats, the furthest from causing harm, and the quickest to be digested.

In the *Sahihayn* (the two Sahih collections): "He (ﷺ) used to be pleased with it." The back meat is very nourishing and produces praiseworthy blood. In *Sunan Ibn Majah*, traced to the Prophet: "The best meat is the back meat."

[Section: The harm of constant reliance on meat]

One should not persist in eating meat constantly, for it causes blood diseases, plethora (excess fullness of the body), and acute fevers.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Beware of meat, for it has a craving like the craving for wine." Malik mentioned it in *al-Muwatta'* from him.

Abqarat (Hippocrates) said: "Do not make your bellies a graveyard for animals."

Ibn al-Qayyim, al-Tafsir al-Qayyim, on Surah 52, verse 23:

Then He declared that wine free from the blemishes of idle talk (lagh) from its drinkers and from the incurring of sin by them. So He said: ﴿There is no idle talk therein, nor any sinful discourse﴾

By "lagh" (idle talk) He negated abuse, quarrelling, abandoning (of one another), obscenity in speech, and drunken brawling.

By "ta'thim" (sinful conduct) He negated all the blameworthy attributes that make the drinker of wine sinful.

Note that He, glory be to Him, said ﴿wa la ta'thim﴾ and did not say "wa la ithm." That is, there is nothing in it that would drive them to sin.

Nor does any of them cause another to sin by drinking it, nor does Allah make them sinful for it, nor do the angels; so they neither engage in idle talk nor incur sin.

Ibn Qutaybah said: it does not take away their intellects so that they engage in idle talk, and nothing occurs from them that would make them sinful.

Then He described their attendants, who go around them, as being like pearls in their whiteness, and like a guarded hidden pearl that no hands have defiled. The service does not remove those excellences, that color, purity and radiance; rather, even while they stand to serve their masters, they are like hidden pearls. In another place He described them: ﴿And when you see them, you think them scattered pearls﴾. In the mention of "scattered" there is an indication of their dispersal across their masters' needs and their service, their going and coming, and the spaciousness of the place, such that they do not need to be gathered together in it because it is cramped.

(Benefit)

These are other than their children. For it is part of the completeness of God Most High's honor toward them that He makes their children attended to along with them, and does not make them servants to them.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned what they will say to one another there, and that they will say: ﴿Indeed, we were before this, among our people, fearful.﴾

That is, we were fearful in a place of safety, among our family, relatives and kin. That fear and apprehension brought us to the point where God bestowed His favor upon us, so we were made secure from what we had feared.

﴿And He protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind.﴾ This is the opposite of the state of the wretched one who used to be joyful among his family.

That man was joyful despite his wrongdoing, whereas these were fearful despite their good deeds.

So God replaced their fear with the greatest security, and replaced the security of those others with the greatest terrors.

And in God, glory be to Him, is the help sought.

Then He informed of their state in the world, that they used to worship God therein. Their worship of Him alone led them to His nearness, His presence, and the place of His honor. And what gathered all of that for them was His piety and mercy, for indeed ﴿He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful.﴾ This is the matter sworn to by those five oaths at the beginning of the surah, and God knows best.

(A benefit)

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, we used to call upon Him before. Indeed, He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful.﴾

This is the supplication of worship, which includes asking, out of desire and awe. The meaning is: we used to devote our worship to Him before.

It was for this that they deserved to be protected from the punishment of the scorching wind, not by mere asking, which is shared between the one who is saved and others, for God is asked by everyone in the heavens and the earth. Success and salvation come only through sincerity in worship, not through mere asking and requesting.

Ponder this repetition and restriction (of the possibilities), which contains the establishment of proof by the nearest route and the most eloquent expression.

He, the Exalted, says: "Were they created from nothing? Or were they the creators (of themselves)?" ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ ... (Qur'an 52:35)

Thus, that a thing be made without a maker, and created without a creator, is impossible and inconceivable to everyone who has understanding and intellect.

Were a man to pass by a barren land with no buildings in it, and then pass by it again and see in it structures, palaces and well-built edifices, there would be no doubt or uncertainty in his mind that a maker made them and a builder built them.

Then He said: ﴿Or were they the creators?﴾ (Qur'an 52:35). This too is impossible: that the servant should bring himself into being and create himself. For one who cannot add to his life after his existence, even with the means of life, not for a single hour, nor a finger, nor a nail, nor a hair, how could he be the creator of himself while in a state of non-existence?!

When both possibilities are invalidated, it is established that they have a Creator who created them and a Originator (Fatir) who brought them into being. He is the true God who deserves their worship and thanks, so how can they associate with Him another god, when He alone is their Creator?

If it is said: what is the place of His saying ﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth?﴾ (Qur'an 52:36) within this argument? It is answered: it is in the best place. For by the first two possibilities He has shown that they have a Creator and Originator, and that they are created. And by the third possibility He has shown that, after they came into being and were created, they are powerless and not creators, for they did not create their own souls, nor did they create the heavens and the earth. And that the One, the Subduer, besides whom there is no god and no lord other than Him, is the One who created them and created the heavens and the earth. He alone is the One who created the dwelling and its inhabitants, the creation of the upper and lower worlds and what is in them.

Some scholars said: The blessings of God upon us in what He has withheld from us of this world are greater than His blessings upon us in what He has extended to us of it.

That is because God did not approve of the world for His Prophet. So, to be among those whom God approved for His Prophet and loved for him is dearer to me than to be among those whom He disliked for him and was angered by.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: It has reached me from some scholars that he said: The scholar should praise God for what He has withheld from him of the worldly desires, just as he praises Him for what He has given him.

And where does what God has given him stand, when its reckoning will come upon him, compared to what God has protected him from and not tested him with, so that it would occupy his heart and weary his limbs? So he thanks God for the tranquility of his heart and the gathering of his resolve.

And it is related from Ibn Abi al-Hawari, who said: Fudayl ibn Iyad and Sufyan ibn Uyayna sat one night until morning discussing the blessings. Sufyan began saying: God has blessed us with such-and-such, God has blessed us with such-and-such, God has done such-and-such to us. And Abdullah ibn Dawud related to us from Sufyan concerning God's words: ﴿We will draw them step by step from where they do not know﴾.

He said: He lavishes blessings upon them and withholds gratitude from them.

Others besides Sufyan said: Whenever they commit a sin, He bestows upon them a blessing. Thabit al-Bunani was asked about istidraj (gradual enticement), and he said: That is the cunning of God against the heedless servants.

Yunus said in its explanation: If a servant has a station with God and he guards it and remains upon it, then thanks God for what He has given him, He gives him something more noble than it.

But if he neglects gratitude, God draws him on gradually, and his neglect of gratitude becomes istidraj.

Abu Hazim said: God's blessing upon me in what He has withheld from me of this world is greater than His blessing in what He has given me of it.

Indeed, I have seen Him give it to peoples, and they perished. Every blessing that does not bring you closer to God is a trial. And when you see God continuing His blessings upon you while you disobey Him, then beware of Him.

(Section)

When you come to the Prophet ﷺ and reflect upon his biography with his people, and his patience for the sake of God, and his endurance of what no prophet before him endured, and the changing of circumstances upon him: safety and fear, wealth and poverty, security and residence in his homeland, and departure from it, and his abandoning (everything) for God, and the killing of his beloved ones and his allies before his eyes, and the unbelievers' harm to him with every kind of harm: by word and deed, by sorcery, by lying, by slander against him and calumny; and yet with all of that he was patient over the command of God, calling to God. No prophet was harmed as he was harmed, nor endured for God what he endured, nor was given what he was given. So God raised his mention, joined his name with His own name, made him the master of all people, made him the closest of creation to Him in means, the greatest of them in standing with Him, and the most listened-to of them in intercession.

Those trials and tribulations were the very essence of his honour, and by them God increased him in nobility and excellence, and drove him by them to the highest stations.

This is the condition of his heirs after him, the most excellent first and then the next most excellent: each has a share of the trial, which God drives him through to his perfection according to the measure of his following of him. And whoever has no share of that, his portion of the world is the portion of one who was created for it and it was created for him; He placed his provision and his share in it, so he eats from it freely and enjoys it until his share from the Book reaches him.

He tests the friends of God while he is in ease and comfortable living; they fear while he is secure; they grieve while he is joyful among his family. He has his concern and they have theirs; he is in one valley and they are in another. His concern is to sustain his standing, to keep his wealth safe, and that his word be heard; whatever follows from that follows, and whoever is pleased is pleased, and whoever is angered is angered.

Their concern is the establishment of the religion of God, the exaltation of His word, the empowerment of His allies, and that the call be to Him alone, so that He alone is worshipped and none other, and His Messenger is obeyed and none other. So God, glorified is He, has in His testing of His prophets, messengers and believing servants a wisdom that the minds of all worlds fall short of knowing.

Has anyone reached praiseworthy stations and virtuous ends except over the bridge of trial and tribulation?

Thus are the lofty aims: if you wish to attain them, cross to them over a bridge of toil.

All praise belongs to God alone, and may God bless Muhammad, his family and companions with abundant, continuous and everlasting peace until the Day of Judgment, and may God be pleased with all the companions of the Messenger of God.

(Benefit)

Al-Marwazi narrated from him that he said: "Every tasbih (glorification) in the Qur'an is a prayer, except for one place. He said: ﴿And during the nights glorify Him, and at the retreat of the stars﴾, two rak'ahs before Fajr, and ﴿and at the retreat of the prostrations﴾, two rak'ahs after Maghrib."
